statement: A pattern of dots grows in hexagonal rings. Stage 1 is a single dot, and each new stage adds a hexagonal ring of dots around the stage before, giving 1, 7, 19 and 37 dots in stages 1 to 4. How many dots are in stage 10?

choices.misconception: I worked out only the ring added at stage 10, 6 x 9 = 54 dots.
I added rings only up to 6 x 8 = 48, which gives stage 9 rather than stage 10.
I added the rings 6 + 12 + ... + 54 correctly but forgot the single dot in the centre.
I thought stage n adds 6n dots, so I added rings all the way up to 6 x 10.

hints: Look at how many dots each new ring adds: 6, then 12, then 18.
The rings grow by the same amount each time, so each stage total is 1 plus the sum of an arithmetic sequence. Work out how many rings stage 10 has and how big the last one is, then add.
Stage 10 has 9 rings around the centre: 6, 12, 18, and so on up to 54.

solutions.reliable: The rings add 7 - 1 = 6, then 19 - 7 = 12, then 37 - 19 = 18 dots, so the ring added at stage n has 6(n - 1) dots. Stage 10 is the centre dot plus 9 rings: 1 + 6 x (1 + 2 + ... + 9) = 1 + 6 x 45 = 271. The transferable idea: a growth pattern is its first term plus the sum of its increments, so find the rule for the increments first.
solutions.elegant: Using the formula 3n(n - 1) + 1 for stage n gives 3 x 10 x 9 + 1 = 271. Check it on stage 4: 3 x 4 x 3 + 1 = 37, as given.

whyOnTest: Figurate number questions test whether you model the growth step by step instead of guessing, and the distractors are the classic off-by-one ring counts.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
